page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached writes scoring in the bottom 25 percent. Geekbench single-core and Passmark CPU scores represent average performance, while complex multi-core workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing show weaker relative results.

Given the hardware profile and benchmark results, the c3d-standard-4 is suited for general-purpose workloads that rely on single-threaded efficiency rather than high-throughput parallel processing or massive memory bandwidth. Appropriate applications include lightweight web serving, text processing, basic cryptography tasks, and small-scale LLM inference using models under 1B parameters. It is less suitable for database operations, large-scale software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling limitations become bottlenecking factors.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, running on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache and advanced vector extensions like AVX-512. While single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng benchmarks, the instance exhibits weaker multi-core scaling and constrained memory bandwidth, with uncached large-block writes averaging 15.16 GB/sec. There is no local storage or GPU acceleration included. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, text processing, and lightweight web serving, but it is not recommended for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded compilation tasks.
